1.explanation:
The only component that needs updating is the TableToolbarSearch function in TableToolbarSearch.js. This component currently destructures out the aria-label prop from rest but never applies it to the container <div>, and then spreads the original rest (including aria-label) onto the inner <Search> instead of the container. To fix the bug you should:
1. In the TableToolbarSearch signature, destructure aria-label from rest into an ariaLabel variable and collect the rest as restProps.
2. Add aria-label={ariaLabel} to the container <div> with role="search".
3. Spread restProps (not rest) into the <Search> component so that only supported props go to the input.
This change will allow users to pass an aria-label to TableToolbarSearch and have it applied correctly to the search container for proper accessibility.
1.bug_scenario: In the Carbon storybook example for DataTable with a toolbar, the search trigger (the div with role="search") does not render the aria-label attribute when you pass one on <TableToolbarSearch>. Visually, the highlighted div shows role="search" and the styling classes but lacks any aria-label, making it inaccessible to screen readers even though the user passed aria-label="Search through table".

2.explanation: The functional component TableToolbarSearch in TableToolbarSearch.js is responsible for rendering the <div role="search"/> container. It currently collects all extra props in `...rest` and spreads them onto the inner <Search> component, so any `aria-label` given to TableToolbarSearch never reaches the search container. To fix the issue, TableToolbarSearch must explicitly destructure `aria-label` from its props and pass it as `aria-label={ariaLabel}` on the outer container <div>.
2.bug_scenario: The TableToolbarSearch component renders its search container as a <div role="search"/> but does not apply any aria-label passed to it. In the storybook screenshot you can see the blue search icon region has role="search" but no accessible name. When you try to add aria-label="Search through table" on <TableToolbarSearch>, that attribute is swallowed (or passed to the inner Search), so the container remains unlabeled and screen readers won’t announce the search region properly.
